subject: Nimbus Retail — workload fingerprint & success plan
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Cheng <alyssa.cheng@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-20 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Nimbus Retail — workload fingerprint & success plan

Hi Alyssa — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can turn the PoC planning into concrete acceptance criteria and an onboarding timeline.

Recap (from our notes):
- Primary use case: checkout fraud detection enrichment (sync scoring) and customer-facing recommended responses (low-latency text generation).
- Two traffic classes: scoring endpoint (high QPS, short responses) and assistant endpoint (lower QPS, longer context).
- Integration: API calls from edge services in us-west, no PII payloads; some SKUs included in examples.

What we need from Nimbus to finalize the traffic intake:
1) RPS baseline & peak: average RPS for scoring + estimated burst factor.
2) Token distributions: median and 95th for both scoring and assistant payloads (we found two example payloads helpful).
3) Concurrency targets and SLOs: target p95 latency for scoring (ms) and assistant (seconds).
4) Example payloads and a short sample request log (last 24–72h) so we can synthesize a realistic replay.

Proposed Redwood deliverables and timeline:
- By EOD Wed (48h): Redwood to provide a proposed PoC success rubric (traffic gates, latency/cost targets) and a draft evaluation plan.
- Next Tue: joint load-replay session and baseline measurements against a pinned model variant.
- Week 2: tuning (batching, quantization recommendation) and cost projection.

Owners: Marcus will lead infra/load tests; Priyom will capture evaluation metrics and make model config recommendations. I'll coordinate the kickoff and handle the PoC doc.

Attachments: I attached a template for request logs and a short example payload set — fill & return when you can.

Ask: Can you share sample request logs and a token-length histogram by EOD Tue? If that's tight, tell us what you can provide and we'll adapt.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0129

[Attachment: nimbus_sample-requests.csv] [Attachment: example-payloads.json]

From: Alyssa Cheng <alyssa.cheng@nimbusretail.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Baker <tom.baker@nimbusretail.com>
Date: 2027-06-20 14:38:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Nimbus Retail — workload fingerprint & success plan

Thanks, Stephanie — great summary and we like the timeline. Quick answers and files attached (see nimbus_sample-requests.csv).

Short answers:
- Scoring endpoint: baseline 350 RPS during business hours, typical burst x3 (weekend sale spikes higher, but we'll limit the PoC to normal/weekend patterns).
- Assistant endpoint: baseline 45 RPS, burst to 120 RPS during marketing campaigns.
- Token lengths: scoring requests median ~40 tokens, 95th ~110 tokens; assistant median ~420 tokens, 95th ~1,200 tokens.
- Concurrency: target p95 latency for scoring = 120ms; assistant p95 = 1.8s.

Files included: nimbus_sample-requests.csv (24h sample), nimbus_token-distribution.xlsx, example-payloads.json. The sample includes a mix of masked user IDs and SKU tags.

Notes:
- We do not send full PII in the payloads; merchant IDs and item hashes are okay.
- We can run a short replay window on a staging API key if Redwood wants to pull traffic directly — need to agree on time and rate limits.

Next steps from our side: schedule the joint replay session (Tom will coordinate with infra), and confirm the PoC success rubric.

— Alyssa
Director, Machine Intelligence
Nimbus Retail
alyssa.cheng@nimbusretail.com

[Attachment: nimbus_sample-requests.csv] [Attachment: nimbus_token-distribution.xlsx] [Attachment: example-payloads.json]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Cheng <alyssa.cheng@nimbusretail.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-21 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nimbus Retail — workload fingerprint & success plan

Alyssa — thanks for the quick data dump, very helpful. I pulled the CSV and did a short pass to validate obvious anomalies. A couple of quick notes before we schedule the replay: 

- The scoring logs show many short requests (<60 tokens) which is consistent. We'll treat 350 RPS baseline and x3 burst as our gating.
- Assistant traffic has a long tail; to keep PoC costs reasonable we'll target a 95th token cap of 1,000 for the initial run and surface any regression alerts if we hit >1,000 tokens in >1% of calls.
- Can you confirm whether retries are client-side or server-side? The sample has occasional duplicate request IDs we want to understand.

Proposed dates for joint replay: Thursday 2027-06-24 10:00–11:30 PT or Friday 2027-06-25 13:00–14:30 PT. We'll provision a temporary staging key and run conservatively to mirror your burst profile.

Deliverable updates: I'll produce the initial performance baseline report within 24h of the replay (CSV + short readout). Priyom will produce the evaluation rubric and suggested model config (batch size, KV cache handling, quantization level) in the same package.

Marcus Lin
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

[Attachment referenced: initial-baseline-template.csv]

From: Alyssa Cheng <alyssa.cheng@nimbusretail.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Baker <tom.baker@nimbusretail.com>
Date: 2027-06-22 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nimbus Retail — workload fingerprint & success plan

On Tue, Jun 21, 2027 at 09:22, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Can you confirm whether retries are client-side or server-side? The sample has occasional duplicate request IDs we want to understand.

Good question — those are client-side retries from our edge (we throttle aggressively at the client and debounce when possible). We'll do a small cleanup on our side and re-generate the sample without duplicate IDs and send before the replay.

Thursday 6/24 10:00 PT works best for us. Tom will send a calendar invite with the staging key window. Looking forward to the run — appreciate the clear owners and timeline.

Best,
Alyssa

[Forwarded message: see attachments sent 6/20]
